issues.failure_explanation: The proof of Lemma th:stability asserts that the CFL condition \eqref{eq:stability} implies a parameter-independent bound $\frac{\wt\gamma_\theta^2}{1+\gamma_\theta^2}\le\mu<1$ and concludes that the constructed norm $\vvvert P\vvvert=\int|V(\theta)^{-1}\wh P(\theta)|_2\,\d\theta$ is equivalent to $\|\cdot\|_{A\times A}$ uniformly in $\eps,\tau,h$. This uniform bound is false. With $\gamma_\theta=\alpha\,[1+\kappa^2(1-\sin(\beta-\thetah)/\beta)]$ and $\wt\gamma_\theta=1-\kappa^2\frac{\alpha^2}{\beta^2}(1-\cos(\beta-\thetah))$, take $\kappa=1$, $h=\eps$ (so $\beta=1$, which satisfies $2\kappa^2|\alpha|\le\beta^2$ for $|\alpha|\le\tfrac12$) and the spectral value $\thetah=1-\tfrac{\pi}{2}$ (so $\beta-\thetah=\tfrac{\pi}{2}$): then $\gamma_\theta=\alpha$ and $\wt\gamma_\theta=1-\alpha^2$, whence $\frac{\wt\gamma_\theta^2}{1+\gamma_\theta^2}=\frac{(1-\alpha^2)^2}{1+\alpha^2}\to1$ as $\alpha\to0$ (i.e. as $\tau/\eps^2\to0$, which the CFL class admits). Thus $\|V(\theta)^{-1}\|_2\le1/\sqrt{2(1-\mu)}$ cannot hold uniformly and the claimed uniform equivalence fails. More strongly, as $\tau/\eps^2\to0$ the amplification matrices converge to $\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}2&-1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$, which has the double eigenvalue 1 with a one-dimensional eigenspace; a norm satisfying the exact conservation $\vvvert P^n\vvvert=\vvvert P^{n-1}\vvvert$ with uniformly bounded equivalence constants would imply uniform power-boundedness $\|G(\theta)^n\|_2\le C$, contradicting the linear growth of powers of the defective limit matrix. Hence the lemma's stated conclusion is false over the CFL class as written. The proof of Lemma lem:stability-cn repeats the same construction (there $\|V^{-1}\|\sim|\gamma_\theta|/(2\sqrt{|\gamma_\theta|^2-1})$ degenerates as $|\gamma_\theta|\to1^+$, which occurs precisely as $\tau/\eps^2\to0$), so the identical root invalidates it as well.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Split the parameter range. For $\tau/\eps^2$ bounded below (say $\tau\ge c_0\eps^2$), $|\gamma_\theta|\ge c>0$ uniformly and the paper's eigenbasis construction yields the norm equivalence with uniform constants, proving Lemmas th:stability, lem:stability-cn and lem:stability in that regime. For $\tau\ll\eps^2$ (where $\gamma_\theta\approx0$), establish the nonlinear stability bound by the standard von Neumann/energy analysis of the limiting classical leapfrog and Crank–Nicolson schemes, to which the weighted schemes converge with lower-order corrections; alternatively, weaken the uniformity quantifiers of Theorems th:MFE, thm and thm:polarized to the regime $\tau\ge c_0\eps^2$. Either contained modification restores all advertised guarantees and rates.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform (in $\eps,\tau,h$) stability guarantees of both weighted schemes — Lemma th:stability, Lemma lem:stability-cn, and the nonlinear stability constant of Lemma lem:stability claimed independent of $\eps,\tau,h$ — are not established for small $\tau/\eps^2$; consequently the uniform-in-$(\eps,\tau,h)$ modulated-expansion and error bounds of Theorems th:MFE, thm and thm:polarized are unproven as stated. The advertised regime ($\tau,h$ large compared with $\eps$, where $|\gamma_\theta|\sim|\alpha|\omega^2$ with $|\alpha|$ bounded away from 0 and the conditioning of $V(\theta)$ is uniform) is not affected.
issues.title: Linear stability lemmas rely on a false parameter-uniform eigenbasis bound, so the claimed uniform norm equivalence (and the uniform error constants) is not established
issues.why_classification: The defect is confined to the regime $\tau\ll\eps^2$ (the classical limit, where $\gamma_\theta\to0$ and the amplification matrices approach the defective limit); in the advertised regime $\tau,h\gg\eps$ the paper's eigenbasis argument is uniform, since $|\gamma_\theta|\gtrsim|\alpha|\omega^2$ with $|\alpha|$ bounded below. A complete resolution — a regime split plus a standard, contained-but-nontrivial stability argument for the classical limit, or a limited weakening of the uniformity quantifier — preserves every advertised guarantee, rate and method; no new global proof architecture is needed and no central result or advertised regime is abandoned.
